concept.name: Delta-neutral trading
concept.definition: A portfolio construction approach that offsets positive and negative deltas so the combined position has near-zero sensitivity to small moves in the underlying's price. Directional risk is neutralized so that other exposures - volatility, time decay, or carry - drive the P&L.
concept.intuition: If an option behaves like 40 shares, holding 40 offsetting shares cancels first-order price risk; what remains is the curvature (gamma), the clock (theta), and the volatility exposure (vega).
concept.mechanics: Compute the net delta of all legs (option deltas summed per contract times multiplier; stock counts one per share) and trade the underlying to bring net delta to zero, rebalancing as prices, time, and implied volatility shift the Greeks.
concept.formula: Delta_portfolio = sum(n_i x Delta_i) = 0, where n_i is the number of contracts or shares and Delta_i the per-unit delta of each leg.
concept.failure_modes: Delta neutrality holds only for small moves: large gaps or volatility spikes change delta faster than rebalancing can track, and a perfectly delta-neutral book can still lose heavily through vega, theta, and funding costs.
concept.misconceptions: That delta-neutral means risk-free; it only neutralizes first-order directional exposure, leaving convexity, volatility, and liquidity risks fully in place.
concept.example: Long 10 puts with delta -0.31 plus long 310 shares gives net delta near zero; after a $1.24 drop the put delta moves to -0.43, so the trader buys 120 more shares to re-neutralize.

citations.source: Charles Schwab, 'Gamma Scalping: A Primer' (Schwab Center for Financial Research)
